latest.title: System Design for Beginners: tips from an ex Amazon Software Engineer
latest.description: System Design felt overwhelming when I started at Amazon. There were too many terms, too much to learn, no clear starting point. After years of building large-scale systems, I now know better what actually matters to design a well rounded system: how to define requirements, build technical foundations, master trade-offs, and prepare for system design interviews. In this article, I will walk you through what I struggled with so you don't have to, and give you a path to improve your System Design skills.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.

trending.title: Introducing Sahara: A Business OS Built on WhatsApp

Everything happens over WhatsApp, the one thing they already know how to use. So that's what I built Sahara on top of: three AWS databases doing real work behind a single phone number, with nothing new for either of them to learn.

trending.title: Are We Merging the Right Models?
trending.description: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned expert LLMs into a single model that handles multiple tasks at once. Standard practice freezes each expert at its best validation checkpoint before merging, but we find this is often the wrong choice. The optimal training duration turns out to be *method-dependent*: simple averaging wants undertrained experts, while sparsification-based methods like TIES reach their best performance with deliberately overfitted ones.

trending.title: 52 AWS Study Guides in 18 Weeks: A Practitioner's Field Notes
trending.description: Some things bother you more than they should. For the "why" and the pitfalls you only discover in production, you're mostly on your own.
